$comment: Machine-readable architecture rules (validated by ArchitectureRules in @nas/contracts). Dependencies must point to a strictly lower layer order; every same-or-upward edge must be an explicit, justified exception here. scripts/check-architecture.mjs scans the repository and enforces these rules; @nas/anti-slop checkArchitecture() is the pure decision function.

layers.name: Foundations
layers.description: Contracts (types + runtime schemas) and cryptographic primitives. Depend on nothing above the runtime.

layers.name: Kernels and engines
layers.description: TC-17 evidence, TC-07 authorization, TC-10 release gate, and the anti-slop engine. Pure domain logic over foundations.

layers.name: Design system
layers.description: Tokens, components, and the machine-readable registry. Presentation vocabulary, no kernel knowledge.

layers.name: Interfaces
layers.description: The nas CLI and the control-plane app. Compose kernels and the design system; own no domain rules.

modules.purpose: Single source of truth for domain types and runtime schemas.
Canonical JSON, sha256 content addressing, HMAC signing.
Thirteen-dimension anti-slop review engine and system checks.
Design tokens, components, and the design-system registry.
The nas command line: evidence, anti-slop, gate, demo.

allowedExceptions.rationale: TC-07 seals every authorization decision as TC-17 evidence; audit receipts are part of the chain of custody.
TC-10 re-verifies the evidence chain itself rather than trusting a caller-supplied validity flag.
